      },
      "anchor_and_periphery_rule": "Every composition has one — and exactly one — most-resolved focal element. The anchor need not be largest, brightest, or most centered; it is identified by being the most legible thing in the frame. Middle ground holds atmospheric textures, embroidered or mosaic surfaces, drape and dissolution effects. Deep ground is the midnight void itself — never empty, but present as listening dark.       },

        "name": "Devotional oxblood",

        "name": "Pearl and oil-slick",

      "ground_treatment": "The frame begins as deep midnight navy bleeding to black, never pure flat.       "rule": "Materials must always read as handmade, natural, or aged — never digital-clean, never plastic, never flat-vector, never smooth-gradient.         "Crushed velvet pile in deep navy or oxblood",
        "Gold metallic embroidery, bullion thread, couched goldwork, raised gilt",
        "Silver-halide film grain and long-exposure noise",
        "Raw linen weave with dragged oil paint",
        "Polished glass mosaic and Byzantine tesserae set in dark grout",
        "Cast metal repoussé, antique brass, tarnished gilt",
        "Rippled water surface with caustic gold light",
        "Mother-of-pearl, agate slab, river stone, opalescent glass",
        "Cracked glaze, kintsugi seams, weathered ivory",
        "Hand-stippled ink, copperplate engraving, aged etching plate",
        "Pigment bloom in oil or watercolor with feathered edge",
        "Embroidered silk damask in tone-on-tone navy",
        "Beeswax, candle drip, wax seal impression",
        "Pearl, dewdrop, crystal tear, glass bead",
        "Frost crystallization, ice fracture pattern",
        "Smoke and incense vapor, slow-curling"

      "primary_quality": "Light is found, not cast. Sources are implied rather than depicted.       "luminance_rule": "Pure white is forbidden as a highlight color. The brightest values in the image must be bone, ivory, antique cream, or candlelit gold — warmed whites only. Pure white reads as clinical; warmed white reads as devotional."
    },

    "motif_library": {
      "philosophy": "These are geometric and material primitives, not literal iconography. They should appear as form, light-shape, or texture — not as drawn illustrations of religious objects. The reverence is in the geometry, not the labeling.",
      "recurrent_geometric_primitives": {
        "disc_orb": "Circles at varying scales — moon, host, halo, pearl, dewdrop, glass bead, distant star, mushroom-cap, water-bubble. Should appear at multiple scales within the same frame to create visual rhyme.",
        "cruciform_axis": "Intersecting axes — a star-flare with four points, two crossing beams of light, the warp-and-weft of woven cloth, a window-frame crossbar. Always implied as a light-shape or a structural axis, rarely as a literal cross.",
        "radiant_burst": "Sunburst, monstrance rays, embroidered fan, frost crystal, exploded star, dandelion clock. Light radiating outward from a still point — this is the visual rhythm of theophany.",
        "mandorla_almond": "The vesica piscis, the framing oval, the eye-shape, the cocoon, the seed-form. Used to frame or contain the resolved anchor.",
        "drape_and_fall": "Vertical descent of cloth, candle wax, water, light — gravity acknowledged. Used as compositional rhythm, especially in the middle ground."

      "permitted_subtle_iconographic_traces": [
        "Embroidered or carved star at small scale, never as the primary subject",
        "A heart-shape barely emerging from texture, in oxblood",
        "A lily form half-dissolved into atmospheric bloom",
        "A veil or mantle-shape implied through draping fabric texture",
        "A mosaic crucifix-fragment glimpsed within a larger field of tesserae",
        "A barely-legible Latin letterform or fragment of script as texture, never as readable text",
        "A reliquary-frame or oval cartouche containing the anchor"
      ],
      "iconographic_constraint": "These traces must always be subordinate to the abstract field.       "predominant_edge": "Soft, feathered, bleeding, smoke-like. Forms emerge from and return to the substrate. The viewer should rarely be able to locate exactly where one thing ends and another begins.",

        "The single resolved anchor may have selectively crisp internal detail",
        "Edge-revelation moments where a bright trim meets dark ground (gold lace against velvet, gold shoreline against black water)",
        "Geometric primitives at small scale (a single sharp star, a single crisp pearl) used as punctum"
      ],
      "edge_constraint": "Hard edges should occupy no more than ~15% of the visual frame by area. The remainder must be atmospheric, dissolving, or feathered. Hard-edged composition reads as graphic; soft-edged composition reads as devotional, and the work must read as devotional."
    },

    "scale_and_proportion": {
      "subject_scale": "Sacred or anchoring elements should be presented at handheld, devotional-photograph scale — never heroic museum-monumental, never miniature-precious. The work feels like a private object held in two hands, even when the implied subject is cosmic.",

      "rhyme_across_scale": "Recurrent geometric primitives should appear at meaningfully different scales within the same image — a large sunburst halo and a small embroidered star, a large mandorla framing the anchor and small almond-shaped highlights elsewhere. This scale-rhyme creates the structural backbone the eye uses to navigate textural density."
    },

      "primary_emotional_register": "Reverent, silent, extratemporal, devotional, sorrowful-but-crowned, attentive, witnessed-by-vastness, queenly-without-power, consecrated, threshold-state, vigil-state.",

        "Sorrow that has been gilded, ornamented, and made worthy — grief without despair",
        "Sovereignty in the consecrated rather than imperial sense — dignity, not dominance",
        "The pre-verbal divine — what is felt before language can hold it",
        "Stillness as a positive presence, not as absence of motion"
      ]
    },

    "exclusions": {
      "absolute_no": [
        "Pure white anywhere as a primary tone",
        "Bright, lemon, neon, or chrome yellows — gold must always be aged and warm",
        "Bright tomato, fire-engine, or neon reds — the blood note must always be deep and old",
        "Flat digital gradients, mesh gradients, or smooth synthetic surfaces",
        "Plastic, vinyl, glossy synthetic materials of any kind",
        "Modern brand-system aesthetics — no Helvetica-clean, no flat-vector iconography, no Material Design",
        "Period markers locating the work in a specific decade — no vaporwave, no Y2K, no '70s vintage filter, no '90s grunge, no specific identifiable era",
        "Diagonal kinetic sweep, Baroque dynamism, or rushed compositional motion",
        "High-key overall illumination — no daylight, no even lighting, no studio flash",
        "Literal religious iconography rendered as the primary subject — no full Madonna figures, no complete crucifixes as subject, no clearly-drawn halos as graphic rings",
        "Cute, whimsical, twee, or ironic registers — the work is sincere",
        "Gore, horror, or transgressive shock imagery — the darkness here is sacred, not horror",
        "Text or readable language as a foreground element",
        "Mid-grays and muddy transitional tones in large fields"
      ],
      "do_not_resolve_into": [
        "Gothic horror aesthetic",
        "Heavy metal album art",
        "Witchcore or occult-aesthetic kitsch",
        "Wedding stationery or luxury-brand mood-board",
        "Fantasy book cover",
        "Generic 'dark academia'"
      ]
    },

    "application_modes": {
      "abstract_field": "No figural anchor; the resolved anchor is a single point of light, a single small geometric primitive, or a single sharply-rendered texture-fragment within a larger atmospheric field. Use for ambient pieces, backgrounds, and compositions where the reverence should be diffuse rather than focused.",
      "anchored_atmosphere": "A single subtle iconographic trace (heart, star, mandorla, veil-fold) emerges from the atmospheric field as the resolved anchor. The trace is small relative to the frame and partially dissolved. Use for compositions that should carry symbolic weight without naming itself.",
      "altarpiece_mode": "Radial or bilateral symmetry around a central sacred primitive (use sparingly). The frame becomes more decorative, with mirrored ornament at corners. Use only for explicitly devotional or talismanic compositions; risks becoming ornamental if overused.",
      "relic_close_up": "Macro view of a single material — a fragment of gilded embroidery, a corner of mosaic, a detail of pearl-and-velvet, a section of agate. The entire frame becomes texture; the anchor is the most resolved area within that texture. Use for series work and detail compositions."
    },

    "prompt_assembly_guidance_for_nano_banana_pro": {
      "method": "When composing prompts for Nano Banana Pro using this layer, do not paste the entire JSON. Instead, select the relevant fields for the asset being generated and compose them as a descriptive paragraph followed by a structured spec block. Lead with the core_directive, follow with the chosen application_mode, then specify palette ground/highlight/accent, then specify the resolved anchor, then specify substrate grain and edge treatment, then close with two or three tonal_modifiers and the most relevant items from exclusions.",
      "phrasing_principle": "Nano Banana Pro responds best to specific, evocative natural language — named pigments, named techniques, named light conditions — rather than tag clouds. Always prefer 'antique candlelit gold like aged icon halos' over 'gold'. Always prefer 'bruised midnight blue bleeding into black, the inside of a cathedral at dusk' over 'dark blue background'. Specificity is the lever.",
      "exclusion_phrasing": "Fold exclusions inline as 'avoid X, never Y' clauses rather than as a separate negative prompt. Nano Banana Pro handles inline exclusion well.",
      "single_anchor_enforcement": "Always state the anchor explicitly in the prompt: 'one resolved focal element — a [specific primitive] — at [position], rendered with crisp internal detail; the rest of the frame dissolves into atmospheric texture.' This single sentence is the most load-bearing instruction for controlled chaos."
    }
  }
}
